name: Feedvisor
summary: AI-driven Amazon and retail-media optimization: dynamic repricing, ad automation and analytics for brands and larger sellers on Amazon and Walmart.
best_for: mid-market and enterprise Amazon sellers with large catalogs where algorithmic repricing and ad optimization move real revenue
skip_if: you're a small seller (rule-based repricers cost a fraction of an enterprise quote), or your margins are set by factors repricing can't touch
honest_knock: The honest structure: Feedvisor publishes no price, so the quote you are given is the only figure that counts — amounts circulating online come from third parties, not from Feedvisor. What it is famous for (the algorithmic Buy-Box strategy that holds prices UP, ad management, analysts) sits on the higher tiers of its own plan comparison: this is enterprise software for serious catalogs. If your Amazon revenue can’t absorb an enterprise quote as a small percentage, simpler repricers are the rational choice.

pricing.notes: Feedvisor publishes no price, and we checked that again on 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-29. feedvisor.com/pricing returns a 404. Their own llms.txt lists every public page and contains no pricing page and no amount. The plan comparison at feedvisor.com/plans does publish a tier structure — Professional, Premium and Enterprise for price optimisation, Feedvisor and Feedvisor Plus for advertising, and a single Enterprise tier for brand optimisation — but every column ends in Request Demo rather than a figure. One correction to what we wrote before: the sentence we attributed to Feedvisor, that pricing is hybrid and varies with catalogue size, ad spend and complexity, is no longer anywhere on their site. The platform has been rebranded to Agentis and that wording went with it, so we no longer put those words in their mouth. Every figure you will read elsewhere, including the roughly $100 a month entry tier and the roughly $1,500 a month for the full platform that we carried before, comes from third parties or from sales conversations rather than from Feedvisor. Treat those as indicative only, and expect a sales call.

cost_traps.label: Quote-only pricing
cost_traps.evidence: No published price: feedvisor.com/pricing returns a 404 and the plan comparison page routes every tier to Request Demo (read 3 Sep 2026)

compare_with.name: Aura or BQool
compare_with.why: the accessible repricer tier — far cheaper, rule-plus-AI based; Feedvisor's edge is holding price ceilings, not just winning races to the bottom

open_questions.question: Can you publish a price, or a starting price, for the plans that are quote-only?
Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?
